claims.text: Humans are susceptible to systematic biases that lead to poor decision-making across domains such as health and personal finance.
Environments can be designed based on human cognitive tendencies to make it easier for people to make beneficial choices.
Choice architecture can guide individuals toward beneficial decisions without restricting their freedom of choice.

evidence.description: The authors explain that 'being human, we all are susceptible to various biases that can lead us to blunder. Our mistakes make us poorer and less healthy; we often make bad decisions involving education, personal finance, health care, mortgages and credit cards'.
The authors state that 'by knowing how people think, we can design environments that make it easier for people to choose what is best for themselves, their families, and their society'.
The text notes that 'thoughtful choice architecture can be established to nudge us in beneficial directions without restricting freedom of choice'.

methodologies.name: Choice Architecture
methodologies.description: Designing decision environments to steer people toward better choices while preserving freedom of choice.
